result.rationale: The handler lowercases only the env-var entries (`process.env.BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.split(",").map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`) but checks `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` against the raw guest email without lowercasing, so 'User@Example.com' bypasses a blacklisted 'user@example.com'. The mechanism described is verifiable in addGuests.handler.ts.

judged_text: Blacklist comparison lowercases the env-var entries but compares them against guest emails verbatim, so 'User@Example.com' does not match a blacklisted 'user@example.com'. Any guest email with different letter casing bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entirely and is added to the booking; the blacklist the operator configured silently fails to block, with no error surfaced.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` are normalized to lowercase (`map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`), but the comparison uses `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` where `guest` is taken verbatim from input (`guests`). Since `guest` is not lowercased, a differently-cased email (e.g., `User@Example.com`) will not match a blacklisted `user@example.com` and will bypass the blacklist and be added.
